# tagents

> Go CLI for managing AI agent fleet across tmux sessions and SSH machines.

No API keys. Uses tmux and SSH from PATH. Reads ~/.ssh/config for machine discovery.

## Commands

- list [--machine <host>] [--all-machines]: List all agent sessions (name, runtime, status, log-idle age, cwd, preview)
- machines: List SSH-config machines with reachability and agent count
- status [--machine <host>] [--all-machines]: Fleet summary counts (total/busy/idle/dead plus log-stale/log-idle summary)
- create <name> [--runtime opencode|claude|codex|pi] [--model M] [--command C] [--cwd DIR] [--prompt MSG] [--repo R --worktree W --branch B] [--from REF] [--wait D] [--force] [--dry-run]: Create a new agent session; optionally create a git worktree first and send an initial prompt (local machine only)
- read <agent> [lines]: Last N lines of agent's tmux pane (default 50)
- log <agent> [lines] [--raw]: Agent session transcript (Claude Code JSONL parsed, default 100 lines)
- where <agent>: Agent's current working directory
- send <agent> <message> [--force]: Send message to agent (warns if busy, --force to override)
- broadcast <message> [--runtime claude|codex|opencode|pi] [--dry-run]: Send to all idle agents
- wait <agent> [timeout] [--log-idle <duration>]: Block until agent is ready (pane-idle OR, when enabled, transcript stale for threshold; default timeout 60s; exit 1 on timeout)
- inject <agent> <file>: Send @<file> to agent
- skill print: Print bundled SKILL.md to stdout
- skill add: Install skill to ~/.claude/skills/tagents/
- docs: Display README.md
- completion [bash|zsh|fish|powershell]: Generate shell completions

## Creating and guiding agents

`tagents create <name>` starts a new tmux session and launches an agent runtime (default `opencode`). It can also prepare a git worktree and send an initial prompt, so spinning off a worker is one command:

```
tagents create PROJ-123 \
  --repo ~/src/example-repo \
  --worktree ~/worktrees/PROJ-123 \
  --branch dev/proj-123 --from origin/master \
  --runtime opencode --model 'haiku[1m]' \
  --prompt "/v/context PROJ-123"

tagents read PROJ-123                          # watch it work
tagents send PROJ-123 "/v/one-shot PROJ-123"  # guide it
tagents wait PROJ-123 5m                       # block until idle
```

`--force` replaces an existing session or worktree of the same name; `--dry-run` prints the resolved plan without changing anything. `create` is local-only.

## Log-idle babysitting

Use `tagents wait claude-worker --log-idle 90s --timeout 30m --json` to babysit workers that may wedge while the pane still looks busy. Readiness is pane-idle OR log-idle >= threshold. The JSON result includes `readyReason`, `logIdle`, and `logIdleFound`, which lets automation distinguish a normal idle return from an empty-turn/context-wedge stall where the JSONL transcript stopped advancing.

## Global flags

  --json, -j         JSON output
  --plaintext, -p    Tab-separated
  --no-color         Disable colors
  --debug, --verbose Verbose stderr logging
  --fields           Comma-separated field selection
  --jq               JQ filter expression
  --quiet, -q        Suppress non-error output
  --machine          Target specific SSH host
  --all-machines     Target all SSH hosts

## Agent name formats

  "sim-1"          Fuzzy match (substring: sim-1 matches oh-sim-1, sim-1-worker)
  "gateway:sim-1"  Pinned machine:name match
  "local:sim-1"    Explicitly local

## Status values

  idle   Waiting for input (green)
  busy   Actively running (yellow)
  dead   Pane missing or empty (red)

## Runtimes detected

Detection uses the pane's foreground process and title first (stable, independent
of which text is visible), then session name and pane content as fallbacks.

  claude    Foreground command 'claude', or name/content markers
  codex     Foreground command 'codex', or name/content markers
  opencode  Foreground command 'opencode'/'vcodex'/'vopencode', pane title 'OC | ...', or name/content
  pi        Pane title 'π - ...' (pi runs as 'node'), a 'pi' name token, or startup header
  unknown   Not detected

## Exit codes

  0  Success
  1  Agent not found or operation failed
  2  Usage error
  3  System error (tmux/ssh unavailable)

## Files

  ~/.ssh/config   SSH machine discovery (Host entries, Include supported)
